report_name: GAO Finds FAA Lacks Real-Time Aviation Cyber Threat Monitoring

vulnerabilities.name: Lack of Real-Time Monitoring and Authentication in Aviation Communication Systems
vulnerabilities.description: A systemic cybersecurity weakness within the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) National Airspace System (NAS) due to the absence of real-time monitoring for electromagnetic spectrum threats like spoofing and jamming. Legacy communication systems, including ACARS and CPDLC, lack robust authentication and encryption, making them vulnerable to manipulation.
affected_products: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS)

identities.name: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)
identities.description: A U.S. government agency found by a GAO report to have significant cybersecurity weaknesses, including a lack of real-time threat monitoring for the National Airspace System (NAS).

identities.name: National Airspace System (NAS)
identities.description: The complex network of systems managing U.S. air traffic, identified as being vulnerable to spoofing and jamming due to a lack of real-time monitoring capabilities.

identities.name: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS)
identities.description: A legacy text-based aircraft communication system that is vulnerable to spoofing and jamming due to a lack of robust authentication and encryption.

identities.name: Controller-Pilot Data Link Communications (CPDLC)
identities.description: A text-based communication system supplementing voice communications for air traffic control, which is vulnerable to spoofing and jamming attacks.
